answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable identity bond before it can earn. Imagine placing a crystal on a mesa above a canyon: the bond stays visible to peers, and slashing knocks it into the canyon if the identity farms rewards with clones. If one identity earns 50 tokens per epoch, a 500-token bond means an attacker spinning up 1000 clones must lock 500,000 tokens, most of it slashed when coordinated cloning is detected. That upfront capital cost makes farming unprofitable.
